text:
Millennium prize problems are falling, rogue agent swarms are doing heists, lab employees are begging for a slowdown…and the most popular AI videos on YouTube are from cope merchants saying it’s all a scam that’s about to collapse.

I get why the message is resonating! It’s comforting to think that the AI is all fake bullshit and the doomers are weird and wrong and life will go back to normal after the bubble pops. But if it doesn’t, these people are doing their audiences a profound disservice.

The discourse from folks working at the Labs today is super weird, even for AI discourse, and suggests to me that everyone is in reaction mode to fast moving events, both in revealed AI ability and in public perception.

GPT-Image 2.5’s control is on another level.

Try these 15 use cases + prompts:

1. Multi-reference merge: image 1 = identity. image 2 = clothing. image 3 = environment. image 4 = composition. use each image only for its assigned role. combine them into one coherent photorealistic scene.

2. Lock the master: this image is the approved master. treat every visible attribute as locked unless I explicitly name it. for future edits, change only the requested variable and preserve everything else.

3. Surgical edit: change ONLY [ELEMENT/REGION]. match the existing anatomy, materials, lighting and perspective. do not modify anything else in the image.

4. Product → full campaign: treat image 1 as the immutable product reference. preserve exact geometry, materials, colors and branding. place it in [SCENE]. change only environment, lighting and camera composition.

5. Controlled A/B testing: create [N] variants of this creative. preserve product, composition, typography and lighting. change ONLY [VARIABLE]. everything else stays locked.

6. Reformat without cropping: recompose this exact image for [ASPECT RATIO]. do not simply crop it. preserve the subject and visual hierarchy while intelligently extending and rearranging the scene.

7. UI → campaign asset: treat the uploaded UI as locked artwork. do not redesign or alter it. place it accurately inside a premium [DEVICE/CAMPAIGN] scene with realistic lighting, reflections and negative space.

8. Artwork → merch: treat image 1 as the exact artwork. preserve its composition and colors. apply it realistically to [PRODUCT], following the material's folds, texture and print behavior. do not redesign it.

9. Storyboard continuity: treat this image as the canonical character, wardrobe and location reference. generate the next shot: [SHOT]. change only camera, framing and pose. preserve everything else.

10. 3D modeling reference: use image 1 as the canonical character reference. generate an exact [VIEW] full-body A-pose reference. preserve silhouette, proportions, materials, accessories and surface details. neutral studio lighting, minimal perspective.

11. Wardrobe swap: preserve identity, proportions, pose, camera, lighting and background. replace only [GARMENT] using image 2 as the reference. preserve its construction, materials, colors and details.

12. Interior redesign: preserve architecture, dimensions, perspective, doors, windows and camera position exactly. change only [ELEMENT] to [NEW DESIGN].

13. Localization: preserve the product, composition, lighting and visual system. replace only the existing text with "[EXACT TEXT]" and adapt secondary environmental details for [MARKET]. add no other text.

14. Sketch → polished visual: rebuild this sketch as a polished [DIAGRAM/INFOGRAPHIC]. preserve every node, relationship and label exactly. improve only hierarchy, spacing, alignment and visual design.

15. E-commerce cleanup: preserve the product exactly. remove the environment and isolate it on [BACKGROUND/TRANSPARENT]. repair only edge details required for a clean catalog image. do not alter color, branding or proportions.

Save these.

The real fun starts when you test that control yourself.
